Stakeholders from the Special Geographic Area backed the bill with no opposition voiced at the hearing.
A stakeholder asked that the Special Geographic Area Development Authority's services under Section 3 cover irrigation systems, not only flood control, sewerage and drainage.

Amendments attach the Bangsamoro Da'wah Center to the Office of the Chief Minister and give it 4 units: training, research and policy development, endowment (Waqf), and administrative and finance.

The Mufti of the Bangsamoro Darul-Ifta was made chair of the Da'wah Council, whose members now include the education ministry, the Development Academy of the Bangsamoro, BPDA, the Bangsamoro Pilgrimage Authority, SPAO and an accredited ulama organization.

points: As filed, the bill cuts the members needed to form a regional political party from 10,000 to 5,000, the share of women nominees from 30% to 20%, and the party seat threshold from 4% to 2%.
It revokes all certifications already issued to sectoral organizations and sectoral wings of parties and requires certifying offices to act on new applications within 15 days.
It has sectoral representatives, except those of non-Moro indigenous peoples, the Ulama and traditional leaders, elected together with the first parliamentary elections through the automated system.

committees: Committee on Amendments, Revision and Codification of Laws
points: The committee held 7 public consultations from 13 to 16 January 2026 across the provinces, Cotabato City and the Special Geographic Area with 1,816 resource speakers, received 8 position papers, and held a roundtable with COMELEC, NAMFREL and LENTE on 18 January 2026.
COMELEC Chairman George Erwin M. Garcia had warned that the Electoral Code and its rules say nothing on what happens if "None of the Above" wins a majority.

Deputy Speakers Baintan Adil-Ampatuan and Ishak V. Mastura backed deleting the option; Mastura also moved to drop the section ordering revised ballots for the 13 October 2025 elections because COMELEC had already destroyed those ballots.
The committee moved the official ballot provision (Section 14) from Chapter 1 to Chapter 2 of Article VII on election day.

points: The bills were filed after the Supreme Court, on 30 September 2025, struck down BAA No. 77 for altering districts after the election period began and for gerrymandering, and ruled that BAA No. 58 does not revive.
The Committees on Local Government and Rules held joint public hearings across the region, including Tawi-Tawi on 6 November 2025 and Basilan on 4 December 2025.
The 6 districting bills were weighed together and Bill No. 415 was chosen as the vehicle, with amendments.

committees: Committee on Finance, Budget, and Management
points: The bill, the FY 2026 Bangsamoro Expenditure Program, proposed P114.08 billion for 27 ministries, offices and agencies.
The committee split into 4 subcommittees, each allowed to act as the mother committee for its agencies, and held hearings from 17 November to 10 December 2025.
The committee found consistently low budget utilization rates in several ministries and offices in the previous year and questioned their capacity to spend.

The Office for Bangsamoro Mujahideen Under Special Circumstances planned to double its beneficiaries from 5,000 to 10,000 while its budget fell by P50 million, so the subcommittee recommended topping up its operating expenses from the OCM contingency fund.
The committee met on 11 December 2025 and heard Bangsamoro Attorney General Bantuas M. Lucman.

The Attorney General advised that the BTA is itself a party to the pending Supreme Court cases and should not be seen pressuring the Court; a formal pleading, not a parliamentary resolution, is the proper way to seek early resolution.
His office said it was filing a manifestation with a motion for early resolution in the Lanang Ali and Macapaar cases.

committees: Committee on Good Government, Accountability of Public Officers and Investigation
points: The Committee on Local Government and the Blue Ribbon Committee held a joint inquiry, under Speaker's Memorandum No. 0225-568, into alleged misuse of Office of the Chief Minister funds tied to the Local Government Support Fund, with help from the finance and interior ministries.
The committee gathered position papers and held a 2-day roundtable in Davao City on 12 to 13 September 2024, where stakeholders backed the leave and raised separation of church and state concerns.
Bill 282 was used as the base text with MP Hashemi Dilangalen's consent, and the pilgrimage leave was cut from 30 days to 22 days.
Pilgrimage was widened to other spiritual or moral journeys so the leave also covers non-believers, and it requires 3 years of aggregate service in the Bangsamoro government or BARMM LGUs.
The rules will be issued by the Chief Minister's office and the Speaker's office with the CSC within 60 days, penalties follow civil service law, and the leave cannot be monetized.

committees: Committee on Finance, Budget, and Management
points: The Committees on Ways and Means and on Finance, Budget and Management held 5 focus group discussions, each over 2 days, with tax experts, LGUs and Islamic finance experts in Cagayan de Oro, Davao City and Manila from May to August 2024, with 648 participants.

Public consultations were held in Cotabato City, Lanao del Sur, Tawi-Tawi, Basilan, the Special Geographic Area, Maguindanao del Norte and Maguindanao del Sur from August to October 2024, drawing 2,367 participants.
The committees received 62 position papers, including 5 from MPs Ubaida Pacasem, Rashdi Adiong, Abrar Hataman, Jaafar Apollo Mikhail Matalam and John Anthony Lim.
The code covers regional taxes and fees, collection of capital gains, documentary stamp, donor's and estate taxes under the BOL, and tax neutrality for Islamic banking transactions.

committees: Committee on Social Services and Development
points: The Committee on Social Services and Development approved the resolution at a meeting on 18 February 2025.
The author added 3 WHEREAS clauses noting it is unclear whether Muslim Filipinos are still stranded in Sudan and that accurate figures are needed to account for everyone affected.
The resolution urges the NCMF, DFA and DMW to give welfare, psychosocial, reintegration and repatriation help to Bangsamoro students and workers hit by the Sudan conflict.

committees: Committee on Social Services and Development
points: Author MP John Anthony Lim told the committee about 3,000 deportees from Sabah arrived in 2024 alone, mostly received in Tawi-Tawi, and that LGUs lacked capacity to give them food and shelter.
Deputy Floor Leader Jose Lorena linked the 'halaw' problem to the unresolved Sabah claim and Malaysian citizenship rules, citing 1.2 to 1.7 million stateless people.

Citing budget limits on creating a new parliamentary committee, the committee amended the resolution so the Special Committee on Filipino Deportees sits under the Committee on Social Services and Development.

committees: Committee on Finance, Budget, and Management
points: The Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management drafted the bill from 2021 with consultants and, in 2023, the Asian Development Bank.

At the 1 September 2025 hearing, Minister Ubaida Pacasem presented the bill, and Atty. Hisham Nazz Ala Biruar of the Parliament's legal service flagged concerns over its self-executory nature and possible conflicts with national law on its reach over LGUs.
MPs asked about fund utilization, nationally funded projects and Shari'ah-compliant provisions; the bill sets a cash-based budget and bars raising the budget above the Chief Minister's proposal.
Amendments were taken up on 3 September 2025; Deputy Speaker Baintan Ampatuan submitted reservations and MP Jaafar Apollo Mikhail Matalam registered a reservation on the amendments.

committees: Committee on Amendments, Revision and Codification of Laws
points: An earlier version, BTA Bill No. 201 drafted under then Labor Minister Romeo Sema, reached the plenary but was archived when the first BTA adjourned in 2022.

At a public hearing in Quezon City on 16 February 2024, House Deputy Speaker and TUCP President Raymond Democrat Mendoza urged quick passage; DOLE officials joined a dialogue in Manila on 4 March 2024.
A technical working group led by MP John Anthony Lim with MPs Nabil Tan, Raissa Jajurie and Jose Lorena met 6 times from March to August 2024 to consolidate comments.

New chair MP Alindatu Pagayao convened labor law experts for a 9-day writeshop in Manila and Cotabato City from 22 July to 2 August 2025 that produced the final draft; the bill drew 8 position papers, including from the UP College of Law Workers and Employees Program and UNI Global Union.

The committee recommended adoption with 24 co-authors added, calling on the MSSD, MILG, MIPA and PSA to set up a regional program for mandatory birth registration, especially for Sama Dilaut/Badjao and other indigenous peoples.
The committee amended the title to cover all indigenous peoples hit by Typhoon Paeng, not only non-Moro indigenous peoples, and corrected MAFAR's name to Agriculture, Fisheries and Agrarian Reform.
It urged MENRE, MHSD, MAFAR, MOH, MSSD and MIPA to work together on the immediate and long-term needs of affected communities, with attention to indigenous peoples' cultural needs.
It asked the Bangsamoro Government for regular progress reports on the response.

committees: Committee on Basic, Higher, and Technical Education
points: The resolution, filed on 17 November 2023, had been approved by the previous education committee and was re-adopted at a joint meeting on 19 June 2025 in Cotabato City.
Author MP Froilyn Mendoza said it aims to strengthen culturally relevant indigenous peoples education for elementary and secondary learners.
Committee chairs MP Ramon Piang Sr. and MP Tomanda Antok backed it as a step toward equity and recognition of indigenous peoples' rights.

committees: Committee on Finance, Budget, and Management
points: Consultations in Lanao del Sur, Basilan and online with the Ministry of Public Works and provincial offices led to adding the MHSD to the listed ministries and requiring ministry websites to link to the regional portal.

At a 21 July 2025 hearing in Cotabato City, BICTO asked to be lead administrator; BPDA, MTIT, MOTC, BEZA, MAFAR, MHSD and MILG backed the bill but raised concerns on sustainability, technical capacity, internet in remote areas, budget and retroactive application.
The committee agreed geo-tagging should not apply retroactively to completed projects but may cover ongoing and future ones.

The joint meeting with the finance committee on 1 August 2025 kept a P20 million appropriation, with P3.5 million for BICTO, P2.5 million each for MPW and the Office of the Chief Minister, and the rest split among 11 other offices.

points: At a 24 June 2025 hearing, National Amnesty Commission officials Atty. Jamar Kulayan and Atty. Mohammad Jamalul Giducos reported that the President had authorized the Commission to issue safe conduct passes to amnesty applicants under Proclamations 403 to 406.
The Commission reported 27 safe conduct passes issued, 7 to MILF and 2 to MNLF members at the 11 June 2025 ceremony, and about 3,000 amnesty applicants as of 24 June 2025.

Because safe conduct passes already protect holders from arrest, the committees dropped the request to suspend warrants and retitled the resolution to commend the President and ask for faster issuance of passes to MILF and MNLF applicants.
Members raised extending amnesty to other rebel groups, more information drives for members who have not applied, and legal help for applicants.

committees: Committee on Finance, Budget, and Management
points: A technical working group led by Deputy Floor Leader Raissa Jajurie handled Bill No. 353 and absorbed MP Laisa Alamia's Bill No. 25 on the same subject.
Public hearings were held in Davao City, Tawi-Tawi, Basilan, Marawi City, Maguindanao del Sur, the Special Geographic Area and Cotabato City from June to July 2025, with stakeholders backing passage.
Jubaira Said of the Basilan Women Initiative Foundation asked that peace and reconciliation education be taught in madaris, public schools and the Alternative Learning System.
Kadayangan Mayor Duma Mascud named ancestral land dispossession as a major driver of conflict in the Special Geographic Area.

A Secretariat survey of 32 BARMM ministries, offices and agencies drew 23 replies; only MILG and CSEA had implemented guidelines for the P7,000 annual medical allowance under MFBM Circular No. 2025-004.
MILG, BYC, MOLE and the Office of the Settler Communities had a drug testing condition in their guidelines or drafts, and all 23 respondents were open to adding one.
MP Kadil Sinolinding Jr. cited a Ministry of Health employee who kept using drugs after warnings and was arrested; the chair cited a purse of shabu found in the MILG parking lot.
The Committee on Rules approved the resolution at its 35th meeting on 14 August 2025 after it ran out of time at the 33rd.

Author MP Rasol Mitmug Jr. said former MPs can explain the parliamentary system to schoolchildren and represent the Parliament on official visits, and that a budget had been raised before the Committee on Accounts.
The committee reworded the resolution so that, rather than the Parliament requesting itself, it authorizes the Speaker to establish the Association of Former Members of the Parliament.

Chair MP Sha Elijah Dumama-Alba said the resolution came from Datu Blah Sinsuat Mayor Raidah Sinsuat's report that local fisherfolk could not sell their catch even to government because of procurement rules.
Atty. Hisham Nazz Biruar, BTA procurement chief, explained that RA 12009 dropped competitive bidding as the default under RA 9184, allowing wider use of negotiated procurement.

A procurement specialist said she had not seen any BARMM agency use community participation procurement; MP Kadil Sinolinding Jr. said the Ministry of Health used it only on valid grounds under COA rules.
The bill was a legislative priority named by former Chief Minister Ahod Ebrahim and was jointly referred to the Rules and Finance committees on 17 September 2024.
The report cites the 2023 National Nutrition Survey finding that 34.3% of BARMM children under 5 are stunted.
A Rules subcommittee chaired by MP Kadil Sinolinding Jr. held roundtable discussions, including in Cotabato City and Zamboanga City on 14 January 2025, and called for position papers.
Position papers came from National Nutrition Council Executive Director Azucena Milana-Dayanghirang, MP Susana Anayatin, nutritionist Bai Nishran Candao and consultant Cecilio Adorna, among others.

committees: Committee on Finance, Budget, and Management
points: At a 12 August 2025 hearing in Cotabato City, stakeholders asked for a clearer awarding process, consistent fund allocation, the MFBM as fund manager, collaboration with Islamic banks and disclosure of fund use.

At a 14 August 2025 hearing in Marawi City, Mindanao State University academics backed the bill but asked that it be reconciled with the national Seal of Good Local Governance and that barangay officials' eligibility be clarified.
The committees met the MILG and MFBM on 13 August 2025 on the budget, then approved it in a joint meeting with the finance committee.

Amendments widen the award from local chief executives to all leaders, add a tie-break vote and a no-awardee rule that keeps unused funds in the Special SEAL Fund, and place the endowment under the Bangsamoro Treasury Office.

reports.recommendation: approval of Bill No. 351 with amendments
points: The bills reapportion the 7 district seats left vacant after the Supreme Court ruled on 9 September 2024 that Sulu is not part of BARMM.

The committees consulted the PSA and COMELEC, held public consultations in every province, Cotabato City and the Special Geographic Area plus sessions with the MNLF and MILF and with provincial governors, and received 91 position papers.

The MILF, in a paper signed by Al Haj Murad Ebrahim, backed Bill No. 351 but proposed 2 districts for Marawi City and another configuration for Cotabato City; Deputy Floor Leader Jose Lorena raised districting of remote islands such as Mapun and Turtle Islands.
On 11 July 2025, Deputy Speaker Omar Yasser Sema moved to defer, saying Sulu's exclusion violated the 1996 Final Peace Agreement; members voted 24 to 2, with 5 abstaining, to proceed.
The committee noted the public wrongly blames the Bangsamoro Government for the delayed Quirino Bridge renovation, which is a DPWH national project.
The project, awarded to Frey-Fil Corporation, is stalled over a P120 million variation order reportedly in the 2026 budget; members questioned a variation order above 10% of the contract amount.

The committee asked the Ministry of Public Works to help with repairs and raise the matter with the Intergovernmental Relations Body; MPW agreed to forward the committee's comments to DPWH through the Intergovernmental Infrastructure Development Board.
The committee cited safety risks and economic losses from the deteriorating Awang to Upi to South Upi to Lebak road, especially in Datu Odin Sinsuat and Upi.

The road is under national jurisdiction, though the public blames the Bangsamoro Government; the Ministry of Public Works committed to raise it at the next Intergovernmental Infrastructure Development Board meeting.
Amendments changed a figure in the first WHEREAS clause from 12.03 to 67.9 and fixed a typo.

points: Republic Act No. 11870 of 2022 already upgraded the Malabang hospital in Lanao del Sur to a 100-bed Level II hospital, but the 2019 Ministry of Health data showed bed occupancy of 300% to 400% with no matching rise in its operating budget.
The Committee on Health approved the bill on 19 June 2025, and a joint meeting with the finance committee in Makati City on 3 July 2025 finalized the funding.
The amendment charges an initial P50 million to the 2025 General Appropriations Act of the Bangsamoro, with later operating costs in the annual budget.

A joint hearing with the finance committee on 17 February 2025 sent the bill back over who runs a BARMM hospital under devolved health services and the Mandanas-Garcia ruling, and over long-term funding.

The committees set an initial P50 million for construction and equipment, with the Ministry of Health to keep giving technical and, if needed, financial support after the hospital passes to the Basilan provincial government.
Management transfers to the province on its request with Ministry of Health concurrence, or after a favorable Ministry of Health assessment done every 5 years.

points: The committee consolidated Bill No. 283, a Tipo-Tipo community hospital bill, into Bill No. 104 after its author MP Mosber Alauddin withdrew it and asked that its authors be added to Bill No. 104.
The Committee on Health held a public hearing in Tipo-Tipo on 30 July 2024 with stakeholders from Tipo-Tipo, Al-Barka and Ungkaya Pukan.
A joint hearing with the finance committee on 17 February 2025 sent the bill back over running a BARMM-managed hospital in a province with devolved health services.
The report notes residents must travel hours to Isabela City for specialized or emergency care, often by tricycle or motorcycle.

points: The Committee on Health held a public hearing in Sibutu, Tawi-Tawi on 2 September 2024 with about 500 residents, officials and health workers; some MPs joined by Zoom because of rough seas.
The committees scaled the upgrade down from a 50-bed Level II hospital to a 25-bed Level I general hospital.
An initial P50 million is charged to the 2025 General Appropriations Act of the Bangsamoro.
MPs Amilbahar Mawallil and Eddie Alih asked the committee to also back a hospital in Sitangkay; MP Baintan Ampatuan reserved further amendments for the plenary.

committees: Committee on Finance, Budget, and Management
points: The Maguindanao Provincial Hospital in Datu Hoffer Ampatuan already offers Level III services but is licensed Level II with 299 beds tied to its staffing, about 1 bed per 3,000 residents against the DOH standard of 1 per 1,000.

At a 17 December 2024 public hearing at the hospital, participants raised funding, difficulty keeping specialists because of security and pay, and patients' costs of travel to General Santos or Koronadal.
Chief of Hospital Dr. Mohammad Ariff Baguindali said many patients come from Pagalungan, Montawal and the Special Geographic Area, and stakeholders asked for a new hospital there.
The amendment charges an initial P50 million to the 2025 General Appropriations Act of the Bangsamoro.

committees: Committee on Finance, Budget, and Management
points: Ministry of Health data showed the Iranon District Hospital has 25 beds against a projected need of 364, with bed occupancy of 154% in mid-2024; MOH said the Iranun Corridor's 364,002 residents need a Level 2 hospital of at least 200 beds and 493 staff.

At a 17 September 2024 public hearing in Parang, Municipal Administrator Usman Ibay III and hospital chief Dr. Harris Macapeges said the hospital was overstretched; residents described deaths caused by delayed care.
Cotabato Regional and Medical Center representatives committed to help with capacity-building.
The amendment charges an initial P50 million to the 2025 General Appropriations Act of the Bangsamoro.

points: The committee approved the resolution at its 23 July 2024 meeting.

It rewrote the resolution from seating a madaris association representative in ministry deliberations on Islamic education to calling on all ministries, agencies and offices to hire 1 Values Transformation Officer (Murshid) to support moral governance.

The Murshid's duties include giving inspirational messages at official meetings, joining deliberations on moral governance and Islamic education, and helping run Values Transformation and Values Enhancement Trainings.

committees: Committee on Environment, Natural Resources and Energy
points: The committee heard the resolution on 22 August 2024 in Cotabato City.

Lake Baranibud lies within the 7 land titles issued under the 1996 Final Peace Agreement, and a Provincial Peace and Order Council meeting with DENR and DAR found it had already been subdivided; the resolution aims to stop further subdivision.
The committee amended the title and resolving clause to urge DAR and DENR to take immediate action to conserve the lake, and added 25 MPs as co-authors.

committees: Committee on Environment, Natural Resources and Energy
points: The committee heard the resolution on 22 August 2024 in Cotabato City.
The proposed Ligawasan Enclave Associative Development program includes a multi-purpose flood control base, nature tourism, and sustainable farming and fisheries enterprises in Ligawasan Marsh.

The committee dropped the request for administrative, technical and financial assistance from the title and added a clause naming MENRE as lead ministry with MAFAR, MHSD, MBHTE, MPW, MSSD, MOH, MTIT, CSEA, NIA and the Bangsamoro Board of Investments.

committees: Committee on Environment, Natural Resources and Energy
points: The committee heard the resolution on 10 May 2024 at the Speaker's Lounge, BTA Building, Cotabato City.
The committee backed a Bangsamoro Electrification Administration as a way to strengthen electric cooperatives and lead rural electrification across the BARMM.
The Committee on Labor and Employment, which shared the referral of Bill No. 270, concurred in the consolidated version with amendments.

The committee ran a public call for position papers from 22 August to 5 September 2024 and received 10, including from Notre Dame University, the Ministry of Social Services and Development, the Ministry of Science and Technology, Labor Minister Muslimin Sema, Indigenous Peoples' Affairs Minister Melanio Ulama and the Bangsamoro Youth Commission.
Roundtable discussions on both bills were held in Davao City on 12 to 13 September 2024, with a policy note from the BTA Legislative Research Division.
The report argues that Moro custom of immediate burial rites and about 4 days of mourning forces workers to use up annual leave or go absent without leave.

The committee first took up the resolution at its 27th meeting on 14 September 2024, where Deputy Senior Minister and BPDA Director-General Mohajirin Ali briefed it for the Committee on the Establishment of the Seat of Government.
The seat of government committee picked Barangay Sarmiento, Parang, in its Resolution No. 001 of 7 March 2024 after a consultation in Parang on 16 April 2024 facilitated by MILG-BARMM.
The site is a 215.89-hectare Bangsamoro Government property near Polloc Port and Ecozone and the Coast Guard District.
Next steps listed were a master development plan and feasibility studies, a 2nd round of community consultation, and preserving the existing Cotabato City government center.

points: The resolution went to the committee's Subcommittee No. 2 on measures addressed to the BPDA, chaired by Deputy Speaker Lanang Ali Jr., which met on 23 May 2024.
The Committee on Public Works, the primary committee, had heard the resolution on 18 July 2023 and approved it with amendments, but held its report pending the Committee on Rules.
The author, MP Baintan Adil-Ampatuan, said a 15-year infrastructure plan was needed because the national Block Grant may shrink after 20 years of the Bangsamoro Organic Law.
The BPDA said it would put the resolution on the agenda of the BEDC Infrastructure Development Committee, chaired by the Ministry of Public Works.

The author, MP Baintan Adil-Ampatuan, proposed archiving the resolution at a Subcommittee No. 2 meeting on 23 May 2024, as it was filed before the second BEDC defense and action had already been taken.
The BPDA reported it had printed an initial assessment report on the 1st Bangsamoro Development Plan 2020 to 2022, with the full assessment due by July 2024.
The committee adopted the subcommittee's recommendation to archive at its 30th meeting on 3 December 2024.
The committee took up the resolution at its 30th meeting on 3 December 2024, presented by its author MP Diamila Disimban-Ramos.
Chair Sha Elijah Dumama-Alba said the measure would be one of the Bangsamoro Government's climate change action initiatives.
MP Eddie Alih noted that schools already hold tree planting on their anniversaries; he, the chair and MP John Anthony Lim asked to be co-authors.
Subcommittee No. 2, chaired by Deputy Speaker Lanang Ali Jr., heard BPDA staff and the Office of the Cabinet Secretary on 23 May 2024.
Isah Abduljalil of the BPDA Monitoring and Evaluation Division said the BPDA was finalising a Comprehensive Bangsamoro Accomplishment Report covering 2019 to 2022.
BPDA's Palawan Mamaon said the report would go to the National Government only with the approval of the Chief Minister and the Parliament, after the chair asked that the Parliament review it first.
The committee adopted the subcommittee's recommendation at its 30th meeting on 3 December 2024.
Subcommittee No. 2, chaired by Deputy Speaker Lanang Ali Jr., took up the resolution with BPDA and Office of the Cabinet Secretary representatives on 23 May 2024.

The author, MP Baintan Adil-Ampatuan, said transition plan matters should come from the BPDA and be approved by the Cabinet before reaching the Parliament, and that updating past targets mattered ahead of the elections.
The committee adopted the subcommittee's recommendation at its 30th meeting on 3 December 2024.

Chair Sha Elijah Dumama-Alba said the Bangsamoro Sports Commission already holds an inter-agency sports festival every year, so the resolution was reworded to support and enhance it rather than urge it.
Deputy Speaker Paisalin Tago asked that the festival be region-wide, run by each province with the Sports Commission, and include cultural sports such as sepak takraw and kasipa sa manggis.
MP John Anthony Lim proposed the new title, 'supporting' the Sports Commission in sustaining the annual festival as part of the BARMM founding anniversary.
On MP Eddie Alih's motion, all members present at the 3 December 2024 meeting were made principal authors.
The committee took up the resolution at its 30th meeting on 3 December 2024, ahead of the January Foundation Day.

Deputy Speaker Paisalin Tago, the Chief Minister's focal person for the Foundation Day celebration in Lanao del Sur, proposed that private establishments, including restaurants, display the Bangsamoro flag.
MPs Eddie Alih, Diamila Ramos and John Anthony Lim supported the measure; MP Lim asked how constituents could take part, such as by displaying flags.
The committee added a whereas clause asking ministries, agencies, offices and LGUs to hold special activities and services with the private sector during the commemorative period.
Subcommittee No. 2 heard BPDA staff and the Office of the Cabinet Secretary on 23 May 2024.

BPDA's Palawan Mamaon said the Bangsamoro Knowledge Portal, launched in 2023, already lists mostly Ministry of Public Works projects funded by the Bangsamoro Government, and a project monitoring and evaluation system was being built to add more.
The author, MP Baintan Adil-Ampatuan, said the portal was incomplete and not updated 5 years after the BARMM's creation.
Since the resolution predated the portal, it was amended to urge the BPDA to enhance, update and maintain its existing online database.
The resolution came from Leanabai M. Sakal-Morales's entry in the 3rd Online Bill and Resolution Drafting Contest of MPs Ampatuan and Mitmug.
BPDA's Palawan Mamaon told Subcommittee No. 2 on 23 May 2024 that the Regional Land Use Committee endorsed the draft Bangsamoro Spatial Development Framework 2024 to 2050 to the BEDC on 17 May 2024.
The framework was prepared with UNDP's SHIELD Programme and UN-Habitat under OCM Memorandum Circular No. 0137 s. 2023.
Because the plan was already drafted, the title and resolving clause were revised to ask that it be submitted to the Parliament for approval.

BPDA's Palawan Mamaon told Subcommittee No. 2 on 23 May 2024 that ministries submit quarterly and annual reports for BPDA to consolidate, but some come in late, and suggested a uniform template for all ministries.
BPDA said it had records of accomplishment reports for 2020 to 2023, that reports for 2019 to 2022 were submitted pending enhancements, and that the BTA 1 report would be finalised by July 2024.

Deputy Speaker Lanang Ali Jr. asked that all accomplishment reports be published and kept in a database; MP Abdullah Hashim asked whether they were on the BPDA Knowledge Portal, and BPDA said they would be posted yearly after the data is cleaned.
MP Baintan Adil-Ampatuan raised concerns about agencies' capacity to report, and the chair agreed to include interventions in the 2025 budget.
The committee discussed the resolution in 3 hearings and approved it on 23 October 2024.
The committee noted that Kulliyah graduates struggle to meet the Bangsamoro Organic Law's requirements for Shari'ah judges, which include Philippine bar membership and years of law practice.
The committee said a Juris Doctor bridging program could help ease the shortage of Shari'ah District and Circuit Court judges and the non-activation of some Shari'ah Circuit Courts.
The committee approved the resolution with no amendments on 27 August 2024.
The author, MP Baintan Ampatuan, said the resolution came from a winning entry by Abdullah Mandungay in her office's youth Bill Drafting Contest.

The committee cited the Supreme Court website showing the 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 5th Shari'a District Court judgeships vacant, and warned the shortage could cause case backlogs and push parties to settle claims outside the courts.
The committee heard and approved the resolution on 23 October 2024.

The committee noted that NBI-BARMM covers only Cotabato City and the Maguindanao provinces (less 4 towns), while Basilan, Sulu and Tawi-Tawi fall under NBI Region IX, Lanao del Sur under the NBI Iligan District Office, and the Special Geographic Area under NBI Region XII.
The committee cited an NBI raid led by the Sarangani District Office in General Santos City that disrupted a budget meeting of officers-in-charge of the 8 Special Geographic Area municipalities.
MP Romeo Sema amended the final resolving clause so a copy also goes to the Intergovernmental Relations Body.
The committee discussed and approved the resolution on 27 August 2024.

The Bangsamoro Attorney General's Office said a PAO national office order of 12 February 2024 had already consolidated all Public Attorney's Offices in the BARMM under PAO-BARMM, and suggested the resolution might be moot.
The committee kept the resolution because the Intergovernmental Relations Body was still waiting for an official letter from DOJ-PAO confirming the transfer.

The committee first deliberated the resolution on 23 May 2023 and agreed to ask the Ministry of Finance, Budget and Management whether a staffing notice (NOSCA) had been issued for the Shari'ah Public Assistance Office.
At a hearing on 27 August 2024, Minister Ubaida Pacasem said the ministry issued the NOSCA for the office's head (Director III) on 2 November 2021, but no head had yet been appointed.
The committee approved the resolution unanimously after that confirmation.

The committee first discussed the resolution on 16 October 2023 and agreed to consider it alongside related resolutions jointly referred to the Committee on Local Government; it took it up again at a hearing on 17 September 2024.

The resolution asks the Supreme Court and the Legal Education Board to let law students in the Clinical Legal Education Program orient barangay officials and Lupon members on the Katarungang Pambarangay law and the limits of their jurisdiction.
The committee noted that lawyers may not take part in barangay mediation and that many barangay officials handle conciliation without legal training.

committees: Committee on Finance, Budget, and Management
points: The 2025 Bangsamoro Expenditure Program as filed totalled P96,696,791,225.73; for the first time since 2019 the committee heard all 27 ministries, offices and agencies itself instead of through subcommittees, from 4 to 28 November 2024 in Cotabato City.
The Ministry of Basic, Higher, and Technical Education got the largest share, P32.14 billion or 33.2%, followed by Public Works at P11.43 billion (11.8%) and Health at P7.44 billion (7.7%).
Public Works fell 35.70% from P17.78 billion in 2024 and Human Settlements fell 44.87% to P624.54 million, while the Bangsamoro Darul Ifta rose 241.05% to P180.38 million.
Budget levels were finalised at a committee meeting in Manila on 9 December 2024, after the Committee on Accounts reported on the BTA's own budget.

committees: Committee on Amendments, Revision and Codification of Laws
points: The bill responds to the Supreme Court's 20 August 2024 ruling in Sinsuat v. Ebrahim that struck down Section 5 of BAA No. 55 because only voters of the new municipality's barangays could vote in the plebiscite creating Sheik Abas Hamza.
MP Ishak Mastura opposed the bill at a committee meeting on 28 October 2024.

At a hearing on 15 November 2024, the IBP Cotabato Chapter, MILG, Cotabato State University and MSU-Maguindanao lawyers backed the amendment, while Datu Odin Sinsuat officials opposed it and proposed turning Datu Odin Sinsuat into a city instead.
The committees adopted the IBP Cotabato Chapter's wording: a plebiscite in the political units directly affected within 60 days, run by COMELEC and paid for by the BARMM government.

The committees adopted the IBP Cotabato Chapter's wording: a plebiscite in the political units directly affected within 60 days, run by COMELEC and paid for by the BARMM government.

points: Subcommittee No. 5, chaired by MP Matarul Estino, asked PRO-BAR and the COMELEC Bangsamoro Electoral Office for comments on 7 May 2024; PRO-BAR sent a report on 20 May 2024.

At a subcommittee meeting on 5 June 2024, PCol. Jibin Bongcayao of PRO-BAR reported 66 gun ban violations, 102 suspects arrested and 80 firearms confiscated at 242 checkpoints during the 2023 barangay and SK elections, and that 1,484 of 2,592 BARMM barangays (57%) were contested.
COMELEC's Atty. Joyce Moran said COMELEC relies on PNP data for election-related violence.

At its 29th meeting on 18 October 2024 the committee found the resolution's purpose already met; author MP Diamila Disimban-Ramos agreed to turn it into a commendatory message for the PNP and COMELEC.
The resolution went to the committee's Subcommittee No. 5 on measures addressed to offices outside the BARMM, chaired by MP Matarul Estino, which met on 5 June 2024.

At a Subcommittee No. 5 meeting on 5 June 2024, author MP Don Mustapha Loong said city and municipal election officers were at Salary Grade 14 to 15 and needed upgrading ahead of the Parliamentary elections.
Atty. Joyce Moran of the COMELEC Bangsamoro Electoral Office welcomed the resolution and said election officers nationwide hold Salary Grade 18.
At its 29th meeting on 18 October 2024, the committee noted Senate Bill No. 857 had been substituted by Senate Bill No. 2817 in Senate Committee Report No. 318 of 11 September 2024.
The committee updated the resolution to cite Senate Bill No. 2817, added a whereas clause on the substitution, and extended it to cover the Bangsamoro Electoral Office.

committees: Committee on Finance, Budget, and Management
points: The Committee on Health held a public hearing on 14 August 2024 at the Meranaw Cultural Heritage Center, MSU Marawi City, presided over by Vice-Chairperson MP Marjanie Macasalong, and took position papers until 22 August 2024.
The committee found Masiu residents rely on ill-equipped rural health units and barangay health stations and must travel to Marawi City for specialised care.

The health and finance committees amended Section 4 to give the hospital an initial P50 million from the Miscellaneous and Personnel Benefit Fund of the 2025 Bangsamoro budget, with later operating funds in annual appropriations.

committees: Committee on Finance, Budget, and Management
points: The Committee on Health held a public hearing in Northern Kabuntalan on 8 August 2024 attended by over 1,000 stakeholders, who backed the bill.

The committee found the town of about 26,000 people on the Pulangi River floodplain relies on a rural health unit, with residents travelling 1 to 3 hours to Cotabato City, Midsayap or Kidapawan for hospital care.
The committees renamed it Northern Kabuntalan General Hospital, cut its capacity from 50 to 25 beds, and had the Ministry of Health and the municipality jointly choose the site.

committees: Committee on Finance, Budget, and Management
points: The Committee on Health held a public hearing on 16 July 2024 at the Datu Blah Sinsuat Municipal Gymnasium, where stakeholders backed the hospital.
The committee found flooding often cuts the coastal town's roads to Cotabato City, leaving residents without medical care for days or weeks.

The committees sited the hospital in Barangay Pura, set at least 25 beds to Department of Health standards, and gave it an initial P50 million from the Miscellaneous and Personnel Benefit Fund of the 2025 Bangsamoro budget.

committees: Committee on Finance, Budget, and Management
points: The Committee on Health held a public hearing on 1 August 2024 at a hotel in Zamboanga City and took written submissions until 10 August 2024.
The committee found South Ubian (population 29,583, poverty incidence 25.27%) has only 5 barangay health units, with Sapa-Sapa Hospital 4 to 5 hours away and Datu Halun Sakilan Hospital 8 hours away.
The committees cut capacity from 50 to 25 beds and renamed it Hadja Jubaira Halun Matba Memorial Hospital, following a South Ubian Sangguniang Bayan resolution presented by MP Eddie Alih.

committees: Committee on Basic, Higher, and Technical Education
points: The committee deliberated the resolution at its meeting on 23 July 2024 and approved it without amendments.

The resolution followed the Supreme Court's 9 September 2024 ruling in Province of Sulu v. Medialdea that Sulu is not part of the BARMM, which left seat allocation and representation for the 2025 parliamentary elections unclear.

Author MP Baintan Adil-Ampatuan cited pending motions for reconsideration, a Supreme Court challenge to the Bangsamoro Electoral Code, only 4 accredited regional parties as of 17 October 2024, and low voter awareness of the new 2-ballot system.

Deputy Chief Minister Hatimil Hassan said the MNLF Central Committee decided on 17 October 2024 that excluding Sulu breaks the government's peace commitments, and that the MNLF would leave the convergence of the 2 peace processes if Sulu is excluded.

Floor Leader Sha Elijah Dumama-Alba said the 7 Sulu district seats should be treated as they are until the ruling is final, and that the Government of the Day would not oppose a request the whole Parliament agreed on.

points: The education and justice committees held a joint meeting on 26 September 2024, a week after the resolution was referred, because of its urgency.
The title was changed to express strong support for the MSU College of Law continuing to provide quality legal education for the Bangsamoro people.
New whereas clauses cite Section 6(b) of the MSU Charter (RA 1387), which mandates the College of Law, and the Legal Education Reform Act of 1993 (RA 7662).
An added clause cites the law's legislative history to argue that chartered state universities and colleges are not covered by RA 7662.

points: The committee recommended the resolution, which encourages Bangsamoro ministries, agencies and offices to set up child-minding centres in or near the workplace, without changes.

committees: Committee on Finance, Budget, and Management
points: The committee recommended P8,206,894,205 in supplemental appropriations, drawn from unutilized prior years' appropriations in the Bangsamoro Treasury, with no amendments.
Ministries may deduct up to 1% for engineering and administrative overhead and up to 3% for administrative costs on projects over P1 million.
Motor vehicle purchases need an Authority to Purchase approved by the Chief Minister on the Finance ministry's recommendation.
The appropriations stay available for obligation until 31 December 2025; unobligated funds then revert to the Bangsamoro Treasury for reappropriation.
The committee met on 22 July 2024 and 30 July 2024 and merged Proposed Resolution Nos. 138 and 420, which both ask Congress to create a province for the Special Geographic Area.
The consolidated resolution urges the 19th Congress to create Kutawato Province from Pahamuddin, Kadayangan, Nabalawag, Old Kaabakan, Kapalawan, Malidegao, Tugunan and Ligawasan.

The committee rejected the name "Moro Province" proposed in Resolution No. 420, saying it historically refers to the whole Bangsamoro homeland and would imply shrinking Moro territory to a single province.

The committee consulted the Ministry of Indigenous Peoples' Affairs on 25 April 2024, then held 7 rounds of public hearings in May 2024, including Upi, Cotabato City, Kabacan, Basilan, Sulu, Tawi-Tawi and Manila.
It gathered 32 position papers, 2 petitions and 5 resolutions, among them 11 from civil society groups, 11 from LGUs and 2 from national agencies.

Basilan participants repeatedly asked that the Yakan be included in Section 3, and Tawi-Tawi stakeholders sought a share of revenue from resources in Sama ancestral domains, equal hiring and a tribal university.
A joint meeting with the finance committee on 18 July 2024 reviewed the Ancestral Domains Fund (Section 98) and appropriations (Section 99).

committees: Committee on Women, Youth, Children, and Persons with Disabilities
points: Chairperson Ramos added a first whereas clause noting that the Shari'ah recommends a 2-year lactation period for infants.
MP Anayatin had local government units added to the offices urged to set up lactation stations under RA 10028.
A study by the Parliament's Policy Research and Legal Service found 242 of 444 resolutions (54%) approved from March 2019 to February 2024 were recognitions, commendations or condolences.
The resolution sets aside time in plenary for MPs to give recognitions and condolences instead of filing resolutions, amending Rule VIII of the BTA Rules.
Sub-Committee No. 1 under Deputy Speaker Omar Yasser Sema took up the measure on 20 and 27 May 2024, with input from Secretary-General Raby B. Angkal and the Plenary and Committee Affairs Department.
The Committee on Rules introduced further amendments at its 25th meeting on 22 July 2024.
CSC-BARMM legal officer Atty. Yasmin H. Abdulkarim attended the committee meeting on 8 April 2024.
The committee learned that BARMM gets fewer Civil Service Examination slots than other regions and that CSC-BARMM is classed as a small organization with limited capacity.
Because the resolution was filed in 2022, the author submitted an updated version, which the committee adopted on 22 July 2024.
Added clauses call for more testing centres, examination slots at par with other regions, and a review of the CSC's structure in the region.

Sub-Committee No. 1 of the Committee on Rules took up the staff and visitor dress code on 20 May 2024 with Secretariat officials including Plenary and Committee Affairs Director Jaime M. Ayub and Bills and Index chief Atty. Badrodin S. Tamama.
On 22 July 2024 the Committee on Rules amended the list of attire deemed inappropriate, and a joint meeting with the Committee on Ethics and Privileges adopted the measure the same day.
New whereas clauses cite the Bangsamoro Organic Law and Rule XXVIII of the BTA Rules, which lets the Speaker order non-members to leave the plenary.
Sub-Committee No. 1 of the Committee on Rules took up the MPs' dress code on 20 May 2024 with Secretariat officials as resource persons.
On 22 July 2024 the Committee on Rules removed the list of attire deemed inappropriate and added a reference to Section 1, Rule XXVIII of the BTA Rules.
The Rules and Ethics committees adopted the amended resolution at a joint meeting the same day.
Author MP Mary Ann M. Arnado proposed an Efficient Use of Paper Rule like those of the COMELEC and the Supreme Court, saying many Parliament documents are reproduced unnecessarily.
Sub-Committee No. 1 asked Secretary-General Raby B. Angkal to lead an impact study; the MIS Division chief, Engr. Mohammad Nizhar Acmad, presented a study on ICT tools to support it.
The committee agreed on a phased shift to paper-efficient practice; MP Mitmug said the aim was to reduce, not eliminate, paper.
Members proposed 13 by 8.5 inch paper for plenary matters, A4 for correspondence, and a new section on margins.

The bill went through 9 committee meetings and a joint review with the finance committee on 21 June 2024.
Section 2 was reworded to stress the Bangsamoro Government's duty under the Organic Law to protect internally displaced persons, and to cover only constituent LGUs.
Secretary-General Raby B. Angkal was invited to the committee meeting on 8 April 2024.

The 2 MPs also had the tracking widened to national government agencies and other stakeholders, not only BARMM ministries and LGUs.
Secretary-General Raby B. Angkal backed the picture gallery at the 8 April 2024 meeting but raised concern over the lack of space in the BTA.
The committee dropped the specific reference to the first BTA Parliament so the gallery covers all BTA Parliament members.
The whereas clause on priority codes was updated from 3 to 5 enacted codes, adding the Electoral Code and the Local Governance Code.

points: The committee took up the resolution at its meeting on 20 February 2024.

points: The committee added a definition of shuhada as those who gave their lives, directly or indirectly, in the armed struggle for Bangsamoro self-determination.
It replaced the proposed Bangsamoro Memorial Council with a 7-member Bangsamoro Memorial Management Board chaired by the Bangsamoro Commission for the Preservation of Cultural Heritage.

Board members come from the public works, trade, education and environment ministries, the Bangsamoro Darul Ifta and the Barira municipal government; the board sets criteria for names on the marker and writes the implementing rules.

points: The committee renamed the burial site in Camp Bushra Somiorang, Butig, Lanao del Sur from a Bangsamoro Historical Shrine to a Bangsamoro memorial site.

It created a Hashim and Mimbantas Memorial Site Management Board chaired by the Bangsamoro Commission for the Preservation of Cultural Heritage, with the public works, trade and education ministries and the Bangsamoro Darul Ifta.
Funding was assigned to the public works and trade ministries and the heritage commission, with an initial P5 million appropriated.

committees: Committee on Agriculture, Fisheries, and Agrarian Reform
points: The committee added funding to the title and replaced Section 3 with definitions of extension services, provincial BAFTI training coordinators, the halal industry and halal food.
It gave the institute a lead role in technical training and short courses on agriculture and fisheries.
Guidelines for extension programs and the accreditation of extension services are to be issued in coordination with the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Agrarian Reform.

committees: Committee on Environment, Natural Resources and Energy
points: The committee heard the resolution on 19 February 2024 at the BTA Session Hall in Cotabato City.
It stressed the BARMM Mindanao River Basin technical working group as a way to tackle the region's perennial flooding and its losses to livelihoods.
The committee held 9 public consultations from 15 to 31 January 2024 across every province and the Special Geographic Area; 3,054 people registered and 135 spoke.
It received 99 position papers, including from 18 MPs and the Cotabato City mayor, and treated MP Adil-Ampatuan's Bill No. 06 on the same subject as a position paper.
Resource persons from the environment ministry's Land Management Service and the Philippine Statistics Authority appeared at the 16 February 2024 meeting.
Members forced divisions of the house 3 times during the period of amendments before the committee approved the bill.

Committee on Finance, Budget, and Management
points: The committee received 27 position papers and treated MP Alamia's Bill No. 22 on veteran mujahideen benefits as a position paper.
Its 5 public consultations in May and June 2023, including MILF and MNLF combatants, drew 1,095 participants, 89 of whom spoke.
Some committee members visited the Aceh Reintegration Body in Banda Aceh, Indonesia, on 5 to 8 July 2023 to study its services for former combatants.
The office was renamed from the Bangsamoro Veteran Mujahideen/Mujahidat Affairs Office to the Office of the Bangsamoro Mujahideen Under Special Circumstance.
The committee backed adopting October as Indigenous Peoples Month in the region.

It recommended writing to the Interim Chief Minister, through the Ministry of Indigenous Peoples' Affairs, to declare 29 October a special non-working holiday marking the 1997 Indigenous Peoples Rights Act.

committees: Committee on Finance, Budget, and Management
points: The committee kept the 2024 budget at P98.47 billion after review by subcommittees of each ministry's proposal.
It cut P3.43 billion from special purpose funds, adding P2.53 billion to ministries, agencies and offices (to P77.30 billion) and P900 million to other special purpose items.
Amendments to the special and general provisions are set out in Annex B.
A sub-committee chaired by MP Baileng S. Mantawil held consultations in Barangay Bugawas on 16 September 2023 and Barangay Taviran on 16 December 2023.

On 18 December 2023 the PSA-BARMM regional director, MENRE land management officials and the acting Maguindanao del Norte provincial treasurer authenticated the population, land and income certifications.
The PSA certified 26,703 people in the 10 barangays, above the 25,000 minimum under the Local Government Code, and 34,229 in the barangays left in Datu Odin Sinsuat.
The committee renamed the new municipality from Datu Balabaran Sinsuat to Datu Sinsuat Balabaran.
It is carved from 13 barangays of Datu Odin Sinsuat, with Tamontaka as the seat of government and a land area of 143,984,505 square meters.
A sub-committee chaired by MP Baileng S. Mantawil held consultations on 16 September 2023 and 16 December 2023.
Pending its internal revenue allotment, the Bangsamoro Government is to give the municipality at least P2.5 million a month.
The committee added Barangay Panatan, making 19 barangays separated from Sultan Kudarat to form Nuling.
A sub-committee chaired by MP Mohammad Kelie U. Antao held consultations in Sultan Kudarat on 14 October 2023 and in Cotabato City on 23 November 2023.

On 18 December 2023 the PSA-BARMM regional director, MENRE land management officials and the acting provincial treasurer authenticated the certifications; the PSA put the new town's population at 38,589.

committees: Committee on Finance, Budget, and Management
points: The committee rewrote the bill to extend the validity of the 2023 Bangsamoro General Appropriations Act to 31 December 2024 by amending Section 50 of BAA No. 32.

Funds obligated by 31 December 2024 for infrastructure, operations and other capital outlays stay valid until fully spent; LGU shares in national taxes stay available until fully released and disbursed.
A new Section 50-A keeps personnel services and general administration MOOE valid only until 31 December 2023 and leaves the Special Development Fund's extension to a separate law.

committees: Committee on Finance, Budget, and Management
points: The committee widened the bill to cover the 2023 Special Development Fund as well as the 2020 to 2022 funds.
The 2020 to 2022 Special Development Fund appropriations stay available for release and obligation until 31 December 2024, and for disbursement until fully spent.
The 2023 Special Development Fund, added as Section 50-B of BAA No. 32, stays available for obligation until 31 December 2025.
The committee took up the resolution at its 4th meeting on 16 October 2023, with members unanimous on the need to organize the Shari'ah High Court in BARMM.
On Deputy Speaker Nabil Tan's motion, the 13 committee members present were made authors, and the resolution was approved unanimously on MP Randolph Parcasio's motion.
Members argued the PHILJA pre-judicature program covers only regular Philippine law subjects, which may not suit Shari'ah courts with their limited jurisdiction under PD 1083.
Instead of asking the Judicial and Bar Council to exempt Shari'ah judge applicants, the committee changed the resolution to ask PHILJA to offer a separate pre-judicature program for them.
The title, the 9th whereas clause and the resolving clause were rewritten to match.

committees: Committee on Finance, Budget, and Management
points: The committees set the Bangsamoro Science High School system to be at par with the Philippine Science High School, under the administrative supervision of the Ministry of Science and Technology, with all campuses inside the region.

They added to the Board of Trustees the chair of the Committee on Science and Technology, the executive director of the Philippine Science High School System and a Muslim religious leader from the Bangsamoro Darul Ifta.

committees: Committee on Environment, Natural Resources and Energy
points: The committee backed, without changes, the resolution directing MENRE to intensify its reforestation programs, especially in landslide-prone areas.

Co-author MP Jose Lorena told the committee's 23 June 2023 meeting that the Bangsamoro Organic Law requires an ad hoc joint body to delineate Bangsamoro waters, and that purse seiners in those waters already earn over P10 billion that should benefit the region.

MPs Eddie Alih, Matarul Estino and Randolph Parcasio described commercial and Malaysian fishing vessels encroaching on municipal waters around the Turtle Islands, Sulu and the Moro Gulf, with officials taking payments and unarmed fisheries enforcers unable to act.
Lorena said vessels caught 15 to 19 km out cannot be apprehended because Bangsamoro waters have not been delineated.
The committee strengthened the title to "strongly" urge NAMRIA to "immediately" finalize the delineation, on motions by MP Ramon Piang Sr. and chair Sha Elijah Dumama-Alba.
The committee changed the title to "urging" rather than "requesting" Congress to create a lone congressional district for Cotabato City.

It added whereas clauses noting that Cotabato City is the seat of the Bangsamoro Government and that past and current representatives of Maguindanao and Cotabato City have filed bills for a separate district.
It added a directive to furnish the resolution to the Philippine Congress-Bangsamoro Parliament Forum.

The committee issued a public call for position papers on 29 June 2023 and processed 10, including from MILG Minister Naguib Sinarimbo, the Bangsamoro Commission on the Preservation of Cultural Heritage, the Unified Bangsamoro Contractors and the Lamsan Group of Companies.
It also studied private members' Bill No. 196 by MPs Rasol Mitmug Jr. and Amilbahar Mawallil and Bill No. 212 by MP Don Mustapha Loong, which proposed holiday economics and a set of 22 holidays.
Recommendations included a BCPCH certification that an event is historic, a master list of local special holidays and a procedure for seeking the Chief Minister's approval of local special holidays.
The committee went through the bill line by line at its 12 July 2023 meeting.

The ministry must submit its report through the Secretary-General within 30 days of the resolution's adoption.

The committee rewrote the resolution to direct the Committee on Health to conduct an inquiry in aid of legislation on the vaccination framework strategy, all types of vaccination and emerging and re-emerging diseases in BARMM, rather than only asking the Ministry of Health for a report.
It widened the focus from COVID-19 to all vaccine-preventable diseases, adding whereas clauses on the national immunization program launched in 1976 with WHO and UNICEF.

FY 2020 and 2021 appropriations for infrastructure, capital outlays and MOOE stay valid for obligation until 31 December 2022, and FY 2022 appropriations until 31 December 2023, each remaining in effect until fully released and disbursed.

committees: Committee on Finance, Budget, and Management
points: The committee turned the proposed buffer fund into the Bangsamoro Revolving Fund for Nationally-Funded Programs, to pay salaries of nationally funded workers when national agencies are late in transferring funds.

The Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management must make the money available when salaries fall due and have it reimbursed once the national funds arrive; a new section states the Bangsamoro Government does not assume the national government's salary responsibilities.

It set the fund at P1 billion, charged to the Contingent Fund, dissolved only after ministries stop drawing on it for at least 2 fiscal years, and required MFBM reports to Parliament on releases and disbursements.
The committee backed, without changes, the call for the Ministry of Health to study procuring low-cost, high-efficiency oxygen generators for the 27 hospitals in BARMM.
The committee deliberated on the resolution at its meeting on 14 March 2023.

It changed the resolution from "requesting" to "directing" the Ministry of Health, and widened it from the Special Risk Allowance, One COVID-19 Allowance and Health Emergency Allowance to all benefits owed to COVID-19 health and non-health workers.
It added the Service Recognition Incentive of up to P20,000 and the 14th month pay to the list of benefits.
The committee backed, without changes, the resolution directing the Ministry of Health to report to Parliament on dengue cases and deaths in the region and its measures to prevent their rise.
The committee took up the resolution at a hearing on 8 March 2023 at the BPDA Conference Hall in Cotabato City.
It found a need to fast-track repairs and maintenance of national roads, bridges and highways in BARMM.

It noted that DPWH, through the Intergovernmental Relations Body, had already responded by setting up a DPWH project management office for national infrastructure in BARMM, discussed at the IGRB meeting in December 2022.
The committee said district engineering offices would fall under DPWH's jurisdiction and that all it could do was support the President's call.

The committee held a public consultation in Cotabato City on 17 April 2023 with 342 participants, including the Maguindanao del Norte governor, the Parang mayor and the Cotabato City vice mayor; at least 26 spoke, largely in support.
It presented a March 2022 feasibility study commissioned by the Ministry of Public Works that found the current Bangsamoro Government Center too small and named Parang the best site for a new center.

It processed 39 position papers, treating as position papers Bills 1, 52 and 96 and Proposed Resolution No. 6 by MPs Baintan Ampatuan and Susana Anayatin, which favoured keeping the seat in Cotabato City or studying the transfer.

The committee renamed the measure the Seat of Government Act of 2023, making Parang in Maguindanao del Norte the seat of the region rather than its administrative capital, and added the Office of the Wali to the offices to be relocated.
The committee discussed the resolution at its 2nd meeting on 2 March 2023, about 6 months after it was referred on 17 September 2022.

The committee unanimously approved sending the resolution to Parliament.

A small group led by chair Sha Elijah Dumama-Alba with Raissa Jajurie, Mary Ann Arnado, Anna Tarhata Basman and Jose Lorena conferred with the Commission on Elections on the Code's wording.

Amendments added a declaration of principles favouring principled regional political parties over personality-based politics and promoting gender inclusivity, and new definitions including turncoatism, reserved seats, sectoral representation seats and non-Moro indigenous peoples.
The committee resolved on 6 March 2023 to recommend approval after 10 days of meetings over 1 month.

committees: Committee on Finance, Budget, and Management
points: The committee also excluded General Administration and Support under MOOE, alongside Personnel Services, from the 2022 appropriations kept available for release and disbursement until 31 December 2023.
It required the MFBM to report releases, obligations and disbursements under the extension to Parliament and the finance committee chair.

It added an amendment to Section 67 of the 2022 budget act requiring ministries to file quarterly financial and physical reports within 30 days of each quarter's end, including to Parliament, with automatic salary suspension for officials who fail to comply.

committees: Committee on Finance, Budget, and Management
Committee on Finance, Budget, and Management
points: The committee kept the 2023 budget total at P85.36 billion after subcommittee hearings on each ministry, agency and office.
It cut the Contingent Fund by P2.03 billion, from P6.84 billion to P4.81 billion, and moved the money to ministries and offices, whose total rose to P70.12 billion.

The largest increases went to the BTA Parliament (P785.39 million), MILG (P780.40 million), MOH (P194.03 million) and MSSD (P180.34 million); the Office of the Chief Minister was cut by P25.66 million and MOTC by P6.03 million.
The committee added Qur'an memorizers, not only reciters, to those recognized under Adopted Resolution No. 97.

It reworded the whereas clauses to say the Office of the Chief Minister recommended a technical working group to carry out Resolution No. 97 and that the awardees listed were those cleared by the validation committee.
It listed all members of the Committee on Rules, including ex-officio members, as principal authors.
